user_situation: A newcomer must add one outbound client to an unfamiliar service without first reconstructing the whole architecture.
intent: Find the repository-specific change sequence, inspect a complete example, and form an evidence-backed initial change plan.

user_needs.question: Which complete existing client should I copy first?
Which parts of the repository will I probably change?
Where is client configuration declared and translated?
Where is the external SDK wrapped and constructed?
Which application-facing interface and operation cross the boundary?
What ordered first implementation plan is supported by repository evidence?
How does this repository observe and contain client failures?
How is the integration verified and where are fakes placed?
Where does the client enter the live service graph?

completion_criteria.description: Every observed candidate is visible, hidden behind disclosure, or excluded with a closed reason.
The user reaches any exact source reference in no more than two actions after choosing a step or example.
The recommended example is complete, production reachable, and grounded in exact source locations.
Configuration, construction, local wrapper, consumer boundary, production operation, application wiring, verification, and observability are all answered.
Generated, test-only, unreachable, standard-library, and stale prose candidates never become a production example.
Every visible repository claim resolves to an exact repository-relative source locator.

state_machine.question_answered: What useful repository task can I start?
What is the repository-specific sequence and best example?
Why is this step needed and where is it implemented?
How does one complete client realize the recipe?
What exact source fact supports the selected claim?
